DOE selects four laboratory robotics projects to build reusable autonomy

Argonne, Brookhaven, Oak Ridge and SLAC lead complementary testbeds, with funding subject to negotiations and future appropriations.

DOE / Newswise ↗8 October 2026English editorial summary
Story

Shared infrastructure for scientific facilities

The US Department of Energy’s Office of Science selected four projects to advance robotics and automation for scientific infrastructure. Intended outputs include open software, interfaces, reusable robot skills, datasets and models, alongside safety methods and experiment provenance. The objective is infrastructure other laboratories can extend, rather than four isolated demonstrations.

Complementary roles across four laboratories

Argonne’s MAESTRO will develop infrastructure that improves through experience. Brookhaven’s DART will examine failures, reliability and skill transfer across robotic platforms. Oak Ridge’s TRACE will connect robots, instruments and data through standardized interfaces. SLAC’s SPIRE will combine sample manipulation, detectors and controls in photon- and electron-science facilities.

Funding and validation are conditional

The announcement identifies $30 million in total funding, including $2 million in fiscal 2026, with later funding dependent on congressional appropriations. Selection starts award negotiations and does not guarantee an award. Success must still be demonstrated through transfer across instruments and laboratories, as well as valid scientific outcomes from automated experiments.
